entries.value: I say what I see in the vicolo.

Gennaro’s scooter. Around eleven at night it stopped outside the door; he left the engine running and went in. Half an hour later he came out, put something under the seat and left. My door is right opposite; I see everything.
She clutches her cross in her palm.
Did you see anything in the night?

Her husband Salvatore’s tin. He was a clerk at the port, at the Carusos’. Before he died he told her, ‘Nunzia, don’t give this tin to anyone; one day the Carusos will want it.’ Last week two men came asking. Nunzia shut the door in their faces.
Do you know about Nunzia’s tin?

· Pinpoint haemorrhages inside the eyelids and on the face; bruising on the inner surface of the nose and lips.
· Cotton fibres in the mouth. The heart tired for her age, but not the cause of death.
· Cause of death: mouth and nose covered with a soft object. Time of death: 23.00–00.30.

Gennaro Russo’s account:

· 28 September: €2,500 cash deposit.
· On his phone, 28 September, from an unregistered number: ‘The other half when the tin arrives. — C.M.’
· Where the number last called: the Caruso Marittima office at the port of Napoli.
The grandson’s scooter stops outside the basso.
The two men who came to the door took it
Under the seat of the grandson’s scooter
The tin wasn’t in the basso.
The men hadn’t collected the tin yet.
It was recorded that the tin was found under the seat of the grandson’s scooter.
Assunta Esposito was questioned; the file was closed as a family quarrel.
Gennaro Russo was arrested. Salvatore Russo’s 212 shipping slips went into bube Napoli’s Caruso file.
The death was deemed natural; Nunzia was buried the next day, and the tin vanished.
Pieter de Vries’s extradition from the Netherlands was requested; the tin went to the port.
The neighbour lives opposite the door; she found the body and described what she saw.

The courier log puts him outside the basso from 22.48 to 23.52, the neighbour inside; under his seat, the tin; in his jacket, fibres from the pillow. He had taken money from Caruso’s office for the tin.
The autopsy shows pinpoint haemorrhages, fibres in the mouth and bruising inside the lips.
The tourist was staying upstairs; nothing shows he went into the basso.
Our family’s business is our concern.
Five thousand, a job. Courier work.

The men gave me five thousand, said ‘bring the tin.’ Nonna wouldn’t give it. She shouted; the neighbours would hear. I held the pillow over her face, just to make her be quiet. Then… she went quiet, for good. I took the tin. I was going to hand it over tomorrow.
You were in the basso before midnight.
At work; I was carrying parcels until midnight. I loved my Nonna. Her heart was weak; everyone knew.
He turns his helmet between his hands.
She was smothered with a pillow
In the Quartieri Spagnoli an eighty-two-year-old lacemaker is dead in her bed. The tin her husband left her is missing.

Gennaro Russo’s courier account, 3 October:

· 14 deliveries between 19.00 and 22.48.
· 22.48–23.52 account on ‘break’; scooter location: Vico Lungo, outside the victim’s basso.
· Deliveries again after 23.58.
71, the neighbour in the basso opposite.
26, the victim’s grandson; a scooter courier.
38, a Dutch tourist staying in the rented flat upstairs.
I’m sorry — I’m only here on holiday.
Pieter de Vries flew back to Amsterdam on the morning flight. He could not be reached again.

My floor is her ceiling. Around 23.10, shouting; a young man’s voice: ‘Nonna, five thousand euros!’ The woman said ‘Mai!’ — never. Then silence. I have a flight tomorrow morning. I don’t speak Italian, but I know those two words.
He tugs at his camera strap.
Did you hear anything in the night?

On the morning of 4 October 2030, in the Quartieri Spagnoli, the lacemaker Nunzia Russo (82) was found dead in her bed in a basso opening onto the street.

Her neighbour opposite, Assunta Esposito, found the body at 07.15: the door opened at six every morning, and it hadn’t. Her grandson Gennaro Russo got the news by phone. The Dutch tourist Pieter de Vries is staying in the rented flat upstairs.
Request permission to search Gennaro Russo’s scooter

Under the seat of Gennaro Russo’s scooter (with the branch chief’s approval):

· An old biscuit tin; inside, 212 Caruso Marittima shipping slips dated 1978–1999; on the back of many, notes in Salvatore Russo’s handwriting.
· On the lid of the tin, a strand of the victim’s lace thread.
· In Gennaro Russo’s jacket pocket, cotton fibres from the victim’s pillow.

The autopsy showed smothering, the neighbour the scooter and what went under its seat, the courier log the break times. The search gave the tin and the fibres. The tourist had heard the quarrel; if he wasn’t asked before the autopsy came, he left on the morning flight.
In Napoli witnesses don’t wait. Ask today who is leaving tomorrow.

Someone at Caruso Marittima wanted the old port slips Nunzia Russo’s husband had left her. When Nunzia refused, her grandson Gennaro was offered five thousand euros. During a courier break at night Gennaro went to the basso; when his grandmother said ‘never’, he pressed the pillow over her face and put the tin under the seat of his scooter.
The embroidered pillow on the victim’s bed; a lipstick and saliva stain in the middle.
An old biscuit tin from under a scooter seat; yellowed shipping slips inside.
The crochet work on the victim’s chair; the hook still in the loop.
